inline.body: The `agent` frontmatter value is interpolated into a filesystem path (`$REPO_ROOT/.agents/agents/$agent.md`) without validating that it’s a safe identifier. If the template/frontmatter is malformed (e.g. contains `/` or `..`), the installer could read and inline unintended files. Consider rejecting any agent name that isn’t a simple `[A-Za-z0-9-]+` token before building the path.

inline.body: `assert_prompt_safe` only runs against the inlined agent body, but `$body` (the command body) plus optional `$preamble`/`$suffix` are also inserted into the same Gemini TOML literal prompt and can therefore trigger the same expansion hazards (`'''`, `!{`, `@{`). Adding a safety check for those fragments here prevents accidentally introducing an expansion sequence via command/template content.

`assert_toml_parses` uses `$(python3 -V ...)` inside a `set -e` script; if `python3` is missing (or otherwise fails), the command substitution can terminate the test before printing the intended diagnostic. Guard `python3` presence (and make the version capture non-fatal) so the failure mode stays readable.

Pull request overview Adjusts the Gemini CLI installation so the two orchestrators (`composer`, `conductor`) work reliably by reaching Gemini as top-level commands (instead of Gemini agents), and mitigates Gemini’s default approval-mode tool stripping by pinning `general.defaultApprovalMode` to `auto_edit`. **Changes:** - Add an `agent: ` key for Gemini command templates and update the installer to inline the canonical agent body into the generated Gemini command TOML prompt. - Stop installing `composer`/`conductor` as Gemini agents and add installer cleanup to remove stale previously-installed copies. - Extend installer tests to validate TOML generation/parsing, inlining behavior, prompt-safety guardrails, stale-file cleanup, and settings merge behavior.
